archetype.name: Pretender (goalie-propped)
archetype.definition: A San Jose team whose 6-5-1 record sits ahead of how it plays at 5-on-5, held up by strong goaltending, an efficient power play and wins that needed overtime.

report.headline: Goaltending and the power play are papering over a team getting outshot nightly
report.take:
San Jose looks like a middle-of-the-pack Pacific team: 6-5-1, fourth in the division, on pace for 89 standings points. The site ranks it 21st of 32, and the underlying play is worse than that. At 5-on-5 the Sharks hold a 41.7 xGF %, 29th in the league, and a 45% shot-attempt share, 27th. They allow 30.1 shots a game, 27th, against a league average of 26.9. A team that gets out-chanced this badly usually does not stay at .500.

Three things keep the record afloat. The first is goaltending, which is new. The goalies are +6.3 GSAx, fourth in the league, after finishing at -25.7 last season. Alex Nedeljkovic leads the way at +4.6 with a .903 save %. The second is a power play converting 26.8%, sixth in the league and well above the 21.2% league mark. Macklin Celebrini drives it with 8 of his 15 points on the man advantage, and Ivar Stenberg has 7 power-play points. The third is close games: most of their recent wins came in overtime, and the Pts vs Goal Diff of +1.4 ranks sixth. Without that, a -0.5 goal differential per game, 25th, would put them below .500.

The numbers do hide one point in San Jose's favor. The 5-on-5 PDO is 96.3, well under 100, so even-strength shooting and saves have run cold rather than hot. The all-situations PDO of 99.9 sits close to normal, because the power play and the penalty-killing goalies make up the difference. Two warnings come with that. This franchise outran its goal differential last year too, finishing +6.1 on Pts vs Goal Diff. And the forwards grade only C-, with nobody on the wings or below Celebrini carrying play: Stenberg and Michael Misa sit near 34-35% xGF. Celebrini is the only skater in the top 20 at his position.

The direction is mixed. The last five games were a break-even 18-18 with scoring up to 3.6 a game, but the last ten were 4-5-1 and -8. San Jose is a real step up from the 20-50-12 team of two seasons ago. It is still a team whose playoff hopes depend on its goalies staying hot and the power play staying efficient, and both tend to cool.

strengths.title: Goaltending has flipped from liability
strengths.body: Both goalies are above expected: Nedeljkovic at +4.6 and Askarov at +2.7, for a team GSAx that ranks fourth after last season's -25.7. The team save % is only league-average, which means the goalies are facing difficult shots and still saving more than expected. The skill looks real, but GSAx this high over a dozen games usually comes back toward the pack.

strengths.title: Celebrini-led power play
strengths.body: The power play converts 26.8%, sixth in the league. It runs through Celebrini, who has 15 points in 10 games with 8 on the power play, and Stenberg, who has 7 power-play points. The man advantage is much of the reason San Jose scores near the league average despite poor 5-on-5 play. Some decline from 26.8% is likely, but the top unit has the talent to stay above average.

strengths.title: Defensemen kept quiet
strengths.body: Opposing defensemen produce less against San Jose than their own averages predict. The Sharks rank sixth in that split, and defensemen account for a smaller share of the points scored against them than the league norm. Opponents are not generating offense through the point against this team.

concerns.title: Out-chanced badly at 5-on-5
concerns.body: A 41.7 xGF % (29th) and 45% CF % (27th) mean San Jose spends most even-strength minutes in its own end. That lines up with a forward group graded C- and a lineup where nearly every regular skater is below 47% xGF. This is a talent and structure problem, not a run of bad bounces, so expect it to persist.

concerns.title: Record leans on overtime
concerns.body: The Sharks are +1.4 on Pts vs Goal Diff, sixth in the league, while sitting at -0.5 a game in goal differential (25th). Most of their recent wins needed overtime. They ran +6.1 on this measure last year too, but that kind of luck is not something a team can count on repeating.

concerns.title: Opposing forwards, especially centers, feast
concerns.body: Opposing forwards outscore their expected points against San Jose, ranking 23rd. Centers take a larger share of the points against than the league norm. This fits a team that loses the possession battle down the middle.

trend.note: The Sharks have hovered around .500 all month without a winning or losing streak longer than two games. The last five were even on goals, an improvement on a -8 ten-game stretch.

weekAhead.headline: Four home games, three against bottom-tier teams
weekAhead.body:
After a long road swing, San Jose comes home for four games. Three of the opponents sit in the bottom seven of the site's rankings. Vancouver is 32nd and 2-10-1, allowing a league-worst 33.5 shots a game and killing just 64.4% of penalties. That is the matchup where San Jose's power play should cash in. Buffalo is 26th, with the league's worst save % at .866 and a 69.2% penalty kill. Calgary is 27th, the league's coldest shooting team at 8.0%, and it allows more points to centers relative to expectation than anyone.

Ottawa is the real test. The Senators are 12th and 8-4-0, allow only 23.3 shots a game (fifth), and carry a 103 PDO. San Jose did beat them 6-2 on the road last week. Anything less than a winning week would be a red flag. Even so, a good week against this schedule would say more about the opponents than about the Sharks' 5-on-5 play.

keyMatchups.title: Sharks power play vs Vancouver's kill
keyMatchups.body: Vancouver kills just 64.4% of penalties, last in the league, and San Jose's power play ranks sixth. The Canucks also give up the most shots in the league. This is the game where the Sharks should run up their numbers.

keyMatchups.title: Buffalo's goaltending vs Sharks volume
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo's goalies have the league's worst save % and are -3.9 GSAx. The Sabres do out-attempt opponents, so San Jose may get fewer shots than usual, but any shots that get through have a good chance of going in.

keyMatchups.title: Celebrini against Calgary's middle
keyMatchups.body: Calgary ranks 32nd at holding centers to their expected points. That suits a San Jose team whose two most-used forwards are centers, Celebrini and Will Smith. Calgary's own power play is fourth in the league, though, so the Sharks need to stay out of the box.

weekAhead.watch: Whether San Jose can control play at 5-on-5 against Vancouver and Calgary, or still gets outshot by weak teams.

restOfSeason.body:
The current pace of 89 points is the optimistic case. Getting there requires the goaltending to stay among the league's best and the power play to stay near 27%, while the team keeps winning close games at an unusual rate. Some of the goaltending improvement is probably real: Nedeljkovic is 14th of 69 on the goalie tab, and anything near average would be a huge gain on last season. Still, a +6.3 GSAx over 12 games is likely to shrink, and the 41.7 xGF % will keep producing more shots against than the goalies can absorb.

The cold 5-on-5 PDO should help somewhat as it rises toward 100, and Celebrini gives the team a real top-line driver. Overall, though, this projects as a sub-.500 team on goal differential that finishes in the low-to-mid 80s in points, short of the playoffs unless the possession numbers improve.
swingFactors: Whether Nedeljkovic and Askarov keep saving above expected

confidence.note: Twelve games is a small sample, but the possession numbers are extreme and match last season's profile.
